sn5.5:0.3: The Discourse about Uppalavaṇṇā Thus I have heard:
sn5.5:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.5:1.2: Then the nun Uppalavaṇṇā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms. After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day, and having entered Blind Man’s Wood,
sn5.5:1.3: she stood at the root of a Sāla tree in full flower.
sn5.5:1.4: Then the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in the nun Uppalavaṇṇā, desiring to drive her out of concentration, approached the nun Uppalavaṇṇā, and after approaching he addressed the nun Uppalavaṇṇā with a verse:
sn5.5:2.1: “Approaching (a tree) blossoming from the top, nun,
sn5.5:2.2: You stay alone at the root of the Sāla tree,
sn5.5:2.3: You are second to none in your beautiful form,
sn5.5:2.4: Young woman, are you not afraid of the scoundrels?”
sn5.5:3.1: Then it occurred to the nun Uppalavaṇṇā:
sn5.5:3.2: “Who is this, a human or a non-human, speaking this verse?”
sn5.5:3.3: Then it occurred to the nun Uppalavaṇṇā:
sn5.5:3.4: “This is the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in me, desiring to drive me out of concentration, who speaks this verse.”
sn5.5:3.5: Then the nun Uppalavaṇṇā having understood: This is the Wicked Māra, replied with these verses to the Wicked Māra:
sn5.5:4.2: Of such a character were to come here
sn5.5:4.3: Not a body-hair would shake or tremble,
sn5.5:4.4: Even alone I am not afraid, Māra.
sn5.5:5.2: or I will enter your stomach,
sn5.5:5.4: (even there) you will not see me.
sn5.5:6.1: I have mastery over my mind,
sn5.5:6.3: I am free of all bondages,
sn5.5:6.4: I am not afraid of you, friend!”
sn5.5:7.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Uppalavaṇṇā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
